analysis.title: GS - Callahan - US TMT Quick Hits - 2 Nov 2026
key_insights: NDX fell about 275 bps intraday to its 200-day moving average. SOX fell about 540 bps intraday and registered a new low close for the second half of the year, below the late-July lows.

NDX is down about 611 bps over the last 3 sessions, its biggest 3-day slide since Liberation Day roughly 20 months ago. Equal-weight S&P (RSP) is up about 1% over the same stretch, and the Russell 2000 is now outperforming the NDX on the year.

Desk flows show little defense across Semis and AI. Risk appetite is weaker in a growing wait-and-see mode, as several catalysts have failed to restart AI/Semis momentum. The market is more discerning on how linear the AI build-out is beyond CY27, which is pressuring multiples.
Oil/crude fell and yields reached about 2-month lows, but the relief only lifted consumer-facing tech (OTAs, Internet, Payments). AI/Tech closed on the lows of the day.

Top client questions: continued weakness in INTC and AMD, why Semis are so heavy, whether the AMZN bounce is sustainable, MRVL and LITE moves, strength in analog semis, and why DDOG, RBRK, MDB and FTNT fell so much.

GS Economics/GIR election preview: data centers are unlikely to stay a campaign theme after the election. Congress might limit data center tax incentives, but a national moratorium is unlikely under any outcome. Congressional focus is expected to shift to AI regulation, where basic federal oversight and self-testing could be codified but restrictive rules look unlikely.

ISM manufacturing rose in October above expectations, with a mixed-to-strong composition: new orders and production increased, employment declined, and prices paid eased slightly. The Goldman Sachs Analyst Index (GSAI) moved the other way, down 6.5pt to 49.1, below 50 for the first time since April 2025.

Apple's fiscal 4Q beat on revenue, iPhone revenue, gross margin and EPS, though services revenue was in line. The stock was up about 30 bps after hours from -2%. Gross margin included about 1pt of tariff refund tailwind and EPS included 5c. Focus for the call is new products, the gross margin outlook into the December quarter, and the revenue guide versus consensus of +6% y/y.
Palantir beat and raised. US Commercial revenue grew 148% y/y, and the full-year US commercial growth guide was raised to above 143% from above 134%. Free cash flow guidance was raised to $4.8-5bn.
Fabrinet rose about 13% after hours on a beat and a guide above consensus for revenue and EPS, citing broad-based demand across multiple programs and new product ramps.

ON Semiconductor fell about 2% after hours, off the lows. Fiscal 3Q AI data center revenue grew 39% q/q and 175% y/y, and the company announced the Ferric acquisition for about $600mn. The 4Q revenue guide midpoint was below consensus, while EPS guidance was in line with consensus.

GIR first take on SBAC: it should trade mixed on a site leasing revenue and tower cash flow miss with EBITDA in line. 2026E guidance was lowered on forex and the Chile and Ecuador asset sales, while the underlying outlook was unchanged and AFFO was raised slightly on lower maintenance capex.
Chart of the day: the S&P 500 low vol index has been negatively correlated to the Nasdaq since the summer, which is unusual in the context of 30+ years of data.

Headline beat and raise with stable US Commercial growth of 148% y/y and a higher free cash flow outlook. The stock was up about 1% after hours.
Beat and guide above consensus on revenue and EPS. The stock was up about 13% after hours.
Results were solid and AI data center revenue grew 175% y/y, but the 4Q revenue guide midpoint sat below consensus. The stock was down about 2% after hours, off the lows.

earnings_insights: AAPL fiscal 4Q reported 11/2: total revenue $114.5bn (+12% y/y) vs consensus $113.47bn (+10.7% y/y). Services revenue $31.573bn vs consensus $31.577bn (up about 10% y/y). iPhone revenue $57.583bn vs consensus $56.49bn (up about 15% y/y). Gross margin 47.9% reported, including about 1pt tariff refund tailwind, vs consensus 47.6%. EPS $2.10 reported including 5c tariff tailwind vs consensus about $2.00.

AAPL operating cash flow was $28 billion in the quarter and $28 billion was returned to shareholders. The call at 5pm ET is expected to cover Duo and new products, the gross margin outlook into the fiscal 1Q, and the revenue guide vs consensus of +6% y/y.

PLTR 3Q reported 11/2: US total revenue +119% y/y (vs +115% y/y last quarter). US Commercial revenue +148% y/y (vs +149% last quarter). US Commercial RDV $6.517bn (+4% q/q) vs $6.238bn last quarter (+27% q/q). Rule of 40 at 158% vs 155% last quarter. Full-year US commercial revenue growth guide raised to above 143% y/y from above 134%. Free cash flow guide $4.8-5bn vs prior $4.5-4.7bn.
FN fiscal 2Q guidance (not yet reported): revenue $1.6-1.65B vs consensus estimate $1.48B, EPS $4.77-4.92 vs consensus estimate $4.43.

ON fiscal 3Q reported 11/2: revenue $1.722bn (+7.4% q/q) vs guide midpoint $1.70bn. Gross margin 41.2% vs guide 40-42%. EPS 90c vs guide 81-93c. 3Q AI data center revenue grew 39% q/q and 175% y/y. Inventories $2,069 million vs $2.047bn last quarter.

ON fiscal 4Q guidance: revenue $1.715-1.815bn (+2.5% q/q at midpoint) vs consensus estimate $1.74bn. Gross margin 41.5-43.5% (up about 130 bps q/q at midpoint). EPS 95c to $1.07 vs consensus estimate 96c. Onsemi to acquire Ferric for $600mn plus contingent considerations.

SBAC reported 11/2: site leasing revenue and tower cash flow missed, EBITDA was largely in line with consensus. 2026E guidance was lowered on tower cash flow and EBITDA due to forex and the sale of Chile and Ecuador assets (closed 9/10). AFFO guidance was raised slightly on lower maintenance capex (GIR first take).

Most asked-about earnings this week: AAPL, PLTR, AMD, ANET, BKNG, DDOG, UBER, APP, EXPE, Unity, FWONK, MCHP, LYV, NET, ABNB. Reporting after the close on 11/3 include ALAB, AMD, ANET, BKNG, DUOL, SWKS, TOST and XYZ, and before the open on 11/3 include SHOP, ETN, DT and UPST.
